utterance: Hello Daniel, I'm the doctor seeing you today. I understand you've hurt your lower back lifting something on the weekend and it's been hard to move. Can you tell me what happened and how the pain has been since then?
reply: I lifted a big pot plant in the garden on Saturday and felt a twinge. By Sunday, I could barely get out of bed. The pain is low on the left side of my back and sometimes goes into my left buttock. It gets worse when I bend or get up from a chair, but it's better when I lie still with a heat pack. It's worse in the evening, but I've been working from home mostly lying on the couch with the laptop. I can walk around slowly.

awards.label: What makes the pain better or worse
Effect on work and daily activities

utterance: That sounds painful. I need to check a few important things. Have you had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs? Any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels, or numbness around your groin or bottom? Any fever, unexplained weight loss, or pain at night that wakes you? Have you had cancer, or been on steroids, or had a fall or accident besides the lifting?
reply: That’s a lot at once. I just want to know what’s going on with my back. Can you start with what you think might be causing the pain?

utterance: I can't say what's causing it until I've asked a few important safety questions and examined you — that's the safest way. Let's take them one at a time. Have you noticed any numbness, pins and needles, or weakness in either leg?
reply: No, legs feel completely normal. I haven't noticed any numbness, pins and needles, or weakness in either leg.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Weakness, numbness or pins and needles in the legs

utterance: Good. Any trouble passing urine, any accidents with your bladder or bowels, or numbness around your groin or bottom?
reply: No, all normal. I haven't had any trouble passing urine, no accidents with my bladder or bowels, and no numbness around my groin or bottom.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Any change in passing urine — difficulty, retention or leaking
Red flag excluded: Any loss of bowel control
Red flag excluded: Numbness around the buttocks, genitals or back passage

utterance: Any fever, feeling generally unwell, unexplained weight loss, or pain that wakes you from sleep at night? Have you ever had cancer, osteoporosis, or taken steroid tablets for a long time?
reply: No, I haven’t had a fever or felt generally unwell, and if anything I’ve put some weight on. The pain doesn’t keep me awake at night, it just hurts when I roll over, but once I’m settled I can sleep. I haven’t had cancer or osteoporosis, and I’ve never taken steroid tablets for a long time.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever or recent infection
Red flag excluded: Unexplained weight loss
Red flag excluded: Pain at night or at rest that keeps him awake
Red flag excluded: Any history of cancer

utterance: Also, does the pain go below the knee into the calf or foot, or is it only into the buttock? Any previous back problems?
reply: The pain stays in the lower back and buttock, doesn’t go below the knee into the calf or foot. I had a minor back tweak about five years ago that cleared up in a week, but nothing like this before.

awards.label: Whether the pain spreads down the legs

utterance: Thanks, that's reassuring so far. How bad is the pain out of 10 at its worst, and what have you tried for it — pain tablets, rest, anything else? Any allergies to medicines, or medicines you take regularly? Do you smoke, and how is your general health?
reply: The pain is about a seven when I move or roll over, maybe a three if I keep still. I've tried rest, heat packs, and some paracetamol — no allergies, just tramadol which made me feel sick and dizzy. I don't smoke, my mood's fine, just frustrated. Work's busy with a big deadline coming up.

finding: Well-looking, comfortable at rest. Not pale, jaundiced or distressed.
Slight lean away from the left. No deformity or skin changes.
Tender over left paraspinal muscles at L4–L5 with some spasm. No bony midline tenderness.
Flexion limited to fingertips at mid-shin by pain; extension mildly uncomfortable; lateral flexion to the right painful on the left.
Power 5/5 throughout. Reflexes normal and symmetrical. Sensation intact. Heel and toe walking normal.

utterance: Your exam looks like a muscle and joint strain in the lower back, not a trapped nerve. Before I talk about treatment, a couple of safety questions. Do you have asthma, stomach ulcers, reflux, kidney problems, or bleeding issues? Have you taken anti-inflammatory tablets like ibuprofen or Nurofen before, and did they suit you? How is this affecting your work and walking day to day?
reply: No, I don’t have asthma, but I do have stomach ulcers and I know anti-inflammatories can make them worse. My kidneys are fine as far as I know. I’ve only taken some paracetamol so far, and it didn’t do much. This is affecting my work because of the deadline coming up, but I can walk around slowly most of the day.

awards.label: Stomach ulcers or indigestion with anti-inflammatories
What treatment or pain relief he has tried so far

utterance: When were the stomach ulcers, and are they still active? Are you on any medicine for your stomach, like a proton pump inhibitor such as Nexium or Somac? Any blood in the stool or black stools recently?
reply: I had them a few years ago, but they’re not active anymore. I’m not on any medicine for my stomach. No blood in my stool or black stools recently.

utterance: One last question before I explain the plan. Do you drink alcohol regularly, and are you taking any other tablets, including over-the-counter or herbal ones?
reply: I have a couple of beers on a Friday and maybe a glass of wine on the weekend. I’m not taking any other tablets, including over-the-counter or herbal ones.

awards.label: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally three times daily with food, short course

utterance:
I've examined your back and your legs. This looks like a muscle strain in the lower back from lifting the pot plant. The muscles beside the spine on the left are tight and tender, movement is limited by pain, and there are no signs of a trapped nerve, a broken bone, or anything more serious. Your legs are strong, feeling is normal, and the nerve stretch tests were fine.

Most people with this get a lot better over one to two weeks, and nearly all settle within about six weeks. A scan, including an MRI, is not needed now and would not change what we do. In the first few weeks, scans often show ordinary wear-and-tear changes that are not the cause of the pain and can cause unnecessary worry. We only arrange a scan if there are warning signs, or if the pain is not improving after several weeks.

Please keep moving gently rather than lying on the couch all day — long rest actually slows recovery. Short walks, changing position often, and a heat pack are helpful. You can keep working from your laptop if you stand up and stretch every half hour or so. Avoid heavy lifting and deep bending for now, but you do not need strict bed rest.

For pain, take two paracetamol tablets (1000 mg) four times a day, regularly, for up to a week — not just when it peaks. Because the pain is still strong and paracetamol alone has not been enough, I have also given you ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day with food, for five days only. Because you have had stomach ulcers, take the esomeprazole 20 mg once a day while you are on the ibuprofen, to protect your stomach. Stop the ibuprofen and contact me if you get stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting, or black stools. Do not take tramadol — it does not suit you. Avoid extra alcohol while on these tablets.

I have referred you to a physiotherapist for movement advice and to help you get back to normal activity.

Please come back sooner, or go to an emergency department, if you develop weakness or numbness in a leg, numbness around the groin or bottom, trouble passing urine or controlling your bladder or bowels, fever, pain that is rapidly getting worse, or pain after a fall. Also see me if it is not clearly improving over the next one to two weeks, and we can review whether any further tests are needed then.

Does that plan make sense, and do you have any questions?
reply: That’s a lot at once. I just want to make sure I understand what I need to do. What’s the next step?

utterance: The next step is simple. Start the tablets today: two paracetamol four times a day, one ibuprofen three times a day with food, and one esomeprazole once a day. Keep gently moving and book the physiotherapist. You do not need a scan now. Come back or go to emergency if you get leg weakness, numbness around the groin, or trouble with your bladder or bowels, or if it is not improving in one to two weeks. Is there anything else you want me to go over?
reply: No, I think that’s all. I’ll start the tablets today and book the physio. I just wanted to make sure I wasn’t missing something.

awards.label: Reasonable differential: Acute non-specific low back pain
Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Cauda equina syndrome
